decisions.subject: Project engine baseline
decisions.question: Which engine baseline should this implementation use?
decisions.decision: Update the project across the board to the latest stable Godot. Official latest-stable verification is recorded separately in the project baseline.

decisions.subject: Development planning priority
decisions.question: How important is job-game takeover readiness for planning?
decisions.decision: Job-game takeover readiness (MA-DOC-006) is critical to the owner and comes first in development planning; it does not reorder the child-facing defect repairs.
decisions.note: Owner, 2026-09-30: the purpose is to take over development of Mermaid Roshan, and including this in the audit is critical. Recorded the same day in master audit section 13 as 'critical to the owner and comes first in development planning'; that line moved to the baseline history on 2026-10-03 without a register entry, so the roadmap lost it. Entered 2026-10-03 by Claude from those two sources; no new owner answer is claimed.

decisions.subject: Chef look and pour (owner acceptance, DL-QA-06)
decisions.question: Does the Chef job look and pour right in the current build?
decisions.decision: No. Owner, 2026-10-03: "Chef pours backwards still" and "Chef still looks bad, lots of overdraw". Chef's look and pour are not accepted.
decisions.note: The pour direction becomes checkable once Codex adds the CR0 probe assertion (stream starts at the rendered spout; spout lowest at full tilt); the look stays an owner judgement.

decisions.subject: Animation production methods
decisions.decision: Allow final animation workflows with identity, motion, provenance and device checks; replace compulsory individually generated still frames for new authorized production.
decisions.question: Final animation workflows

decisions.subject: Animation cleanup
decisions.decision: Use Aseprite as the bridge when possible to clean results, preserving approved polished 2D identity.
decisions.question: Aseprite bridge

decisions.subject: Animation production routing
decisions.decision: Default local setup for character design/animation and objects, with APIs for cinematic scenes. This preference does not commission character redesign, a 3D medium change, paid jobs or installation of every candidate.
decisions.question: Local versus API

decisions.subject: Roshan sprite orientation
decisions.question: Q1: is left and right only still the standard for gameplay swimming?
decisions.decision: Sprites need left and right orientation only, with no up or down orientation; standard swimming uses left and right views (confirms the 2026-09-16 two-view swim direction).

decisions.subject: Roshan animation production workflow
decisions.question: Q3: V1 or V2 shot card?
decisions.decision: Production runs through LTX locally, by a script run by Codex, with frames transferred through Aseprite for in-game use. Grok handoffs and shot cards are test documents digested to examine the workflow, not final references; the owner assumes V2 is higher quality and asked for an audit.

decisions.subject: Roshan animation scope
decisions.question: Q4: may gameplay animation be painted limited animation?
decisions.decision: No limited animation: make a rich, comprehensive set of Roshan animations. Develop test animations, workflow and style first, then analyse every room and game for right and wrong animations, then polish and refine the product.

decisions.subject: Sky Lagoon travel
decisions.question: Q5: how does Roshan travel on land in the Sky Lagoon?
decisions.decision: In the Sky Lagoon Roshan still swims, with a different animation from the sea: slower, more modest travel.

decisions.subject: Roshan animation template
decisions.question: Goal statement, with Q6 on the uncommitted strict-rule note
decisions.decision: Goal: a template for developing all future Roshan animations from the game and its context; the handoff analyses each scene and Roshan's interactions, decides whether an animation should be generated and hands it to the appropriate model. The uncommitted strict-rule note is a work-in-progress rule; this process describes the workflow.

decisions.subject: Roshan character animation: whole-figure frames
decisions.question: Review of the 2D-deformation wave (revision 1), where a cut-out arm moved over a body taken from another drawing with per-part delays.
decisions.decision: Rejected: "No arm moves as a single figure, the whole body moves at once, drawn as a whole frame." No limb moves as a separate piece; every frame is one whole drawing of the figure and the whole body moves together.

decisions.subject: Roshan animation: one constant size
decisions.question: Review of the whole-frame bending wave (Claude revision 2, assets_src/cinematics/claude_whole_frame_wave_20261005).
decisions.decision: Rejected: "This is worse than the previous results, roshan mutates in size still." Roshan keeps one size through an animation, including her head, arms and hands, not only her overall figure.

decisions.subject: Sprites drawn whole, as a single unit (game-wide)
decisions.question: Review of the wave studies, whose frames were built from stacked or separately warped pieces.
decisions.decision: "There are also significant overdraw issues, sprites need to be drawn whole, as a single unit, in this game." Each sprite frame is one whole drawing; no part layers, stacked copies or cross-fades.

decisions.subject: Mermaid Pool: Rumi's rise
decisions.question: QP-1: Rumi rises twice: once in the room, then again in the 17-second video. Keep both, or drop one?
decisions.decision: "No, only one." Rumi rises once. The owner-selected d1_pool_clean clip, which cannot be altered (DL-CIN-16), keeps the rise; the room's own rise and greeting are removed.

decisions.subject: Day One dirty-room look
decisions.question: QP-2: Should the other rooms lose their code-drawn dirt and wash the same way, as each gets its own painted dirt?
decisions.decision: "Only when dirty objects are specifically being cleaned, which is different from gathering dirt or freeing the seahorse." Which rooms and effects this changes waits for the owner's choice of reading (QP-2a); no room changed on it yet.

decisions.subject: Castle under Day One story clips
decisions.question: QP-3: Should the castle keep drawing underneath while a story video plays? That is what makes the video's layering high.
decisions.decision: "No." The castle and its voice caption stop drawing while a full-screen Day One story clip plays; the castle stays the open surface for game logic.

decisions.subject: Whole-figure Aseprite retake priority
decisions.decision: Prioritize a tested retake workflow on the 8 GB card with Aseprite to identify and correct frames. Regenerate coherent whole-figure motion including shoulder, torso/dress, hair and tail; registration anchors do not freeze the body.
decisions.question: Owner-directed whole-figure retake priority; already present in the decision view, now reconciled to its JSON register.

decisions.subject: Constant figure scale and Aseprite continuity filter
decisions.decision: Roshan should retain static world size. Use Aseprite to filter continuity errors and anchor the complete figure at multiple corresponding places per redraw for scaling. Preserve pose-dependent whole-figure motion.
decisions.question: Owner: "Why does mermad roshan grow and shrink in this? She should be a static size"; "Aesprite is meant to filter out these continuity errors, anchor the figure at multiples places per redraw for scaling. continue."

decisions.subject: Persistent animation size drift and prior Grok control
decisions.decision: The size problem remains despite improvement. Reuse the controls that fixed the same issue in earlier Grok handoffs; Aseprite must filter continuity errors at multiple figure anchors.
decisions.question: Owner: Problem is still present, if improved. We were able to fix this same issue in the previous grok handoffs, and I am unsure why we are struggling here.

decisions.subject: Remaining internal size/focus errors and different corrective workflow
decisions.decision: Size changes remain subtly visible and the figure shifts in and out of focus. Analyze corrective workflows; regeneration through a different workflow is permitted. Existing footage is not accepted by this direction.
decisions.question: Owner: Still present, if subtle. Also, the figure shifts in and out of focus. Analyze potential solutions to these problems, regeneration is not a problem if done through a different workflow to correct the erros

decisions.subject: Actual structural-control trial
decisions.decision: Commission a trial of the preferred structural-control workflow after the size/focus analysis. This requests generation/testing, not creative acceptance of the result.
decisions.question: Owner: make a trial

decisions.subject: Fashion Designer Roshan: persistent cosmetics, unlocks and disguise games
decisions.decision: The cosmetic feature redresses recurring characters across the game with persistent effects, includes unlockable outfits throughout play, and teaches later disguise through dress-up games. This supersedes the initial working assumption that all clothes are freely available.
decisions.question: Owner: This game has persistent effects. You can redress characters that appear throughout the game using this feature, we'll have unlockable outfits throughout the game too. The fashion designer job will be involving dress up games for disguise, happens later in the game

decisions.subject: Roshan's special dress before the party and Iko Iko/Ember King scene
decisions.decision: Roshan puts on a special dress before the party, prior to the Iko Iko/Ember King scene. This commissions a scoped pre-party clothing beat; garment pixels, implementation and acceptance are not established by the direction.
decisions.question: Owner: Roshan should put on a special dress before the party, so prior to the iko iko ember king scene

decisions.subject: Roshan rig pilot: the rig drives the LTX guides
decisions.question: Which deterministic-rig pilot to build, given the 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-07 whole-frame, whole-sprite and constant-size rules?
decisions.decision: Chose "Rig drives the guides": track the LTX take, solve it onto a fixed-length rig, and use the rig's poses as proportion-locked guides for the next whole-frame LTX take.

decisions.subject: Claude may render this pilot's guides and preview
decisions.question: For this pilot, may Claude render the rig's guide images itself instead of writing them up for Codex?
decisions.decision: "Yes, render them": a one-time exception to the 2026-09-30 written-handoff rule, covering only the rig pilot's guide images and previews.

decisions.subject: Rig pilot: one rules-off test run, then rules back
decisions.question: How to trial the deterministic rig against the existing Roshan animation rules?
decisions.decision: "Trial two test runs, one that completely ignores these rules for purposes of testing, and then if there are problems or shortfalls with the drafts that are analyzed, introduce these rules back again. The game was previously incapable of animating in this way, I suspect that it may be, but permit claude to trial using a different approach." Scope: the rig pilot's run 1 only; the whole-frame, whole-sprite, no-Roshan-rig and written-handoff rules remain binding for production and run 2.

decisions.subject: Rig pilot run 1: whole-body acting, blink, hair flow, no frame artifacts
decisions.question: Review of rig pilot run 1 (rules-off Godot rig, revision 1).
decisions.decision: "This is acceptable as a rough take, but mermaid roshan is frozen otherwise. Give her a full body natural movement that accompanies the hand raise, have her blink, make her hair flow slightly in the water. It's progress" and "There are also a lot of frame-by-frame artifacts present currently". Scope: the rig pilot's run 1 (revision 2).
